newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS RETREAT FROM HIGHS IN LATE TRADING.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS RETREAT FROM HIGHS IN LATE TRADING.

text.p: Belgian bonds retreated from earlier highs on Friday, returning to little changed levels by late afternoon as players held back from opening new positions ahead of the long weekend.
Markets in Belgium and France are closed on Monday for the Armistice Day remembrance holiday.

By 1600 GMT the ten-year benchmark 2006 OLO yield was 6.05 percent, unchanged from the previous close after climbing to 6.03 percent earlier. Its spread over equivalent Bunds widened to 16 bp at one point then shrank back to an unchanged 13.
December bond futures slipped three bp to 119.77.
"The yield curve steepened a little this morning then it flattened, and I see more flattening ahead," one dealer said.
"The short end looks quite expensive, particularly three year bonds."
Dealers said there had been some domestic buying, but also foreign selling coming in.

U.S. Treasuries were expected to dictate the trend in the short term, with all eyes now on U.S. producer prices Wednesday and consumer and retail sales Thursday, as well as the Federal Reserve's policy making FOMC meeting on November 13.
